<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **48** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**33** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90cea476dedee4bb2586f60b4f469bba67904cf3`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`, `objectName (symbol, 57 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **38** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90cea476dedee4bb2586f60b4f469bba67904cf3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dd81a5b7033b335484e5e3154f069d978710b9ac` — the merge of head `d65e2b13435df92ed4ed9b1e1c81ce0f98b98ca3` into base `90cea476dedee4bb2586f60b4f469bba67904cf3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dd81a5b7033b335484e5e3154f069d978710b9ac && git checkout dd81a5b7033b335484e5e3154f069d978710b9ac
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 90cea476dedee4bb2586f60b4f469bba67904cf3 d65e2b13435df92ed4ed9b1e1c81ce0f98b98ca3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 90cea476dedee4bb2586f60b4f469bba67904cf3 && git merge --no-ff d65e2b13435df92ed4ed9b1e1c81ce0f98b98ca3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90cea476dedee4bb2586f60b4f469bba67904cf3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 90cea476dedee4bb2586f60b4f469bba67904cf3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review: E2 #31673, head d49c1e0d · 2026-11-09T00:58Z**

Verdict: **CHANGES REQUIRED**, on two items, both in `ActionsFacet.packageScopedHandler`'s fallback.
- Neither item is reachable today, because no door passes `callerPackageId` until G1. They are the rule G1 turns on, so they are fixed here.
- Everything else passes.

**Item 1: two host-bound handlers become "not found" instead of a refusal (red line 2).**
- `hostBound.length === 1 ? hostBound[0] : undefined` turns two or more candidates into `undefined`, and `executeAction` then throws ``Action '…' on object '…' not found``.
- That is a refusal reported as absence, naming nobody.
- Required: with two or more, refuse (409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, as the declaration door does), naming each handler's owner.
- Add a test that is red without it.

**Item 2: the environment slot is not host-bound (red lines 1 and 2).**
- `handlerOwnerPackageId(p) === p` also admits entries in the `ENVIRONMENT_ACTION_COORDINATE` slot. Those are the handlers `resyncAuthoredActionsNow` registers as `'metadata-service'` for environment-authored actions.
- So when the resolved holder B has no handler in its own slot, B's declaration can run the handler of the environment's own same-key action. That is another holder's code, which the PR says never happens.
- Host-bound means plugin code, the platform: the `sys`-like rule I gave R2 for owner-less functions (6729484996).
- Required: the fallback considers only plugin-registered handlers. Exclude the `''` slot and every `app:` owner, and pin it with a test that is red without the fix: B's declaration with no own handler, plus an environment-authored handler of the same key, never runs the environment's.

**Passes:**

| Red line | Reading |
|---|---|
| 1. Never loosens | Handlers are keyed `(package, objectName, name)`. A no-package call still reads the bare map unchanged; #31697's interim B is pinned and commented. A package call dispatches the **resolved declaration's** holder coordinate (`actionHolderCoordinate`), so a closure dependency's action runs its own handler. Overrides bind in the base coordinate's slot as well as the bare map, and `removeActionsByPackage` prunes both. |
| 2. Ambiguity reported, never guessed | Declarations for a package caller go through R over `actionOwnerScopedRegistry`: the object's own owner key first, else object-less. A refusal never falls through to object-less holders, and the door answers 409 with `candidates`. There is no second resolver. |
| 3. Independently releasable | No resolver import in the engine, so `./core` stays clean and the core-boundary ratchet is green. The narrowing is declared for D3 (a) and the outside-closure holder (6728487836), 0 first-party / 0 reachable. The same-object-pair census is 0 on all four compositions. The changeset carries the ADR-0087 disposition. |

When both are in, send me the head and I will re-check only those two items. The surface is not governed, so seat 4 lands it after that.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d49c1e0db28fcd706743bd1fb3dc542cba3dd11a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/action-handler-coordinate.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-package-addressing.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/bound-action-collision-report.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-actions.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json (generated ledger, read not reviewed) + packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`packageScopedHoldersOf`, `getPackageScopedItem`, `getEnvironmentScopedItem`), packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts (`handlerOwnerPackageId`), packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts, packages/objectql/src/core.ts, packages/objectql/src/core-boundary.ratchet.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (the authored-action resync bind), packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md, docs/adr/0150-behavioural-metadata-addressed-by-package-objects-keep-the-literal-prefix.md

Rendered 2026-11-09T01:14Z on the net diff of `d49c1e0d` against `origin/main` (merge-base `35a9c694`, 12 files, +885/-27), card #31673 with every comment through 6729690154, and the head's check-runs. Prose face not reviewed: `.changeset/31673-action-engine-by-package.md` (its two declaration lines are read in ②).

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, judged against the tree:

1. **`ObjectQL#executeAction(objectName, actionName, ctx, options?)`** gains an optional fourth parameter (`ExecuteActionOptions.packageId`). Additive on the class; a call without it reads `this.actions` byte-for-byte as `main` does (`engine-actions.ts` `executeAction`). **Right.** The spec contract `IObjectQLEngine.executeAction` (3 parameters) is not widened; see ④ N2.
2. **`registerAction`** now places every registration in its owner's package coordinate (`packageActions`, keyed `actionHandlerCoordinate(owner)` then `OBJECT:NAME`) and then runs the unqualified-slot code unchanged (replace, #24472 warning naming both owners, the #30065/#30542 override-beneath arm). **Right**, and the #31697 interim is pinned in both packages (`[#31697 interim]` cases) with the code comment citing #31697 as ruling 6728550494 asked.
3. **`registerActionOverride`** binds in the base's coordinate and the unqualified slot. **Right** for every first-party caller: the resync always passes `action.overrides?.package` as `base` (`plugin.ts` 4307). The no-`base` branch is ④ N1.
4. **`removeActionsByPackage`** prunes both indexes and drops an emptied coordinate. **Right.**
5. **`listRegisteredActions`** is unchanged and enumerates the unqualified slot only. A second package's coexisting handler is invisible to every reader of it. **Wrong for the package-keyed dispatch** (④ F2, N4).
6. **`@objectstack/objectql` main barrel** gains `resolveActionByPackage`, `actionOwnerScopedRegistry`, `actionHolderCoordinate`, `actionHandlerCoordinate`, `ENVIRONMENT_ACTION_COORDINATE`, and the types `ActionPackageQuery`, `ExecuteActionOptions`. The lean `./core` entry is untouched: `engine-actions.ts` newly imports `bare-name-one-holder.js`, which `registry.ts` (already on `./core`) imported on `main`, and `action-handler-coordinate.ts` imports no resolver. **Right** (ADR-0076 D2 holds by construction; CI did not conclude on this head, below).
7. **`resolveRouteActionDeclaration`** gains optional `callerPackageId`; its answer gains `refusal` and `packageId` (`RouteActionDeclaration`). Not on the runtime barrel. Without `callerPackageId` (or with `''`) every rung is `main`'s. **Right.**
8. **`executeRegisteredAction`** gains optional `packageId`, threaded from `handleActionsRequest` as `declarationPackageId`. **Right**; see F2 for the gate that does not see it.
9. **`/actions` door**: a new 409 arm (`standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus(409)`, `candidates`) reachable only when the route passes `callerPackageId`, which no route does (verified: the only `callerPackageId` call sites in the diff are tests). Every request today gets `main`'s answer. **Right.** Note for G1: D5 words the 409 candidates as qualified addresses; here they are `PackageScopedHolder` objects. G1's door spells the address.
10. **A withheld declaration stays withheld**: when the protocol's execution read withholds a disabled package's item (#25308), `resolveRouteActionByPackage` answers `action: undefined` and the route 404s "no declaration" before any dispatch. **Right.**
11. **Changeset**: `@objectstack/objectql` patch, `@objectstack/runtime` patch, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. Level and marker **right** (②).
12. **Gate verdicts on this head** (read 2026-11-09 after 01:03Z): `Lint & Repo Gates` success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, `Check Changeset` success, `PR-body guards` success, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (PR leg) success, `Test UI` success. **Not concluded**: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1/8…8/8)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Live E2E UI` are `cancelled`, and the aggregate `TypeScript Type Check` reads `failure` as the aggregate of those cancelled lanes (it ran 01:02:25Z to 01:02:27Z, two seconds after the lanes were cancelled). Both workflow runs (42542800595, 42542800552) conclude `cancelled`: the branch received `bff4bd5b` at 01:01:27Z. So on `d49c1e0d` the type-check, build and core-test families carry no CI verdict; the dev's local readings (objectql 11674 passed, runtime 10397 passed, tsc clean) are the dev's, not the gates'. This record does not stand in for those gates, and the head is superseded: the newer head needs its own record.

### ② Semver level

- **Level**: `patch` on both packages is right. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no authorable key, value or type moves (no `packages/spec` edit; the card forbids one). The ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right: nothing stored or authored is renamed or retired.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`** on the PR body and the changeset, read by `clause2-line.mjs` as `declared / no / narrowing`. Judged:
  - The **arm** is right: D3 (a) (a package caller whose only holder on the object is an environment-authored action is refused naming the environment) and the outside-closure package holder are refusals of what the bare slot serves today, declared with the dev's counts (0 environment-authored action items and 0 outside-closure first-party callers on showcase, crm, multi-package, todo, the branch's own readings, not re-measured here). The same-object no-package pair is declared unchanged and is #31697's.
  - The **value**. The grammar's question is 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」. Read literally, +14 lines of new exports on a published package's barrel and an optional parameter on `executeAction` enlarge a public surface, which would spell `yes (narrowing)`. Three things decide it `no` here: (i) ADR-0150's execution plan defines Clause-② for this epic as "whether the slice changes a published contract (spec, protocol, SDK, a door's request or response)" and sets E2 `no`; nothing in that list moves (no spec, no protocol, no SDK, and the door's response is unchanged for every request a client can make today); (ii) the precedent is R, merged under the same ADR with 30 new export lines on the same barrel and `Clause-②: no` (`.changeset/31575-package-scoped-resolver.md` at 0ebb0801); (iii) the choice has no gate effect: `record-recognisers.mjs` maps a `narrowing` arm on `yes` or `no` to this same face and `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, and the level follows `Metadata-protocol` alone (`patch` either way). **`no (narrowing)` stands.** The exports are internal plumbing for `@objectstack/runtime` and the G children; the changeset names them, which is the right place.
- One contract this diff does **not** widen and should have somewhere: `IObjectQLEngine.executeAction` in `packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts` keeps three parameters while the dispatcher now calls four on `ql: any`. Out of this card's file surface by the claim; ④ N2 files it.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry of os-dev-report 6729690154:

- **OQ1, "a package call whose own coordinate holds no handler: which handler runs?" — built A (the one host-bound handler, else not found), recommended A.** Answered: **A, corrected.** Running the one handler bound by host code (owner undefined) or by a plugin is right: a declaration's `target` is bound by host code with no package, platform packages in the `sys` namespace are in every closure and their handlers are plugin-bound, and with exactly one such handler nothing is picked between. But the `''` coordinate also holds the authored-action resync's handlers (`actionHandlerCoordinate('metadata-service')` is `''`), and those are environment-authored actions (bucket 4), which D3 (a) refuses to a package caller. So A as built reaches an environment-authored action's body for a package caller through key rotation; ④ F1 names the path and the fix. Option B (own handler only) would break every target-bound first-party action the moment G1 passes a package, so it is not the answer.
- **OQ2, the new public names — keep (A) or rename.** Answered: **keep.** `resolveActionByPackage` / `ActionPackageQuery` follow `resolvePackageScopedName` / `PackageScopedQuery`; `actionHolderCoordinate` and `actionHandlerCoordinate` name the two halves the module doc names; `ENVIRONMENT_ACTION_COORDINATE = ''` agrees with R's sentinel reading (`''` is a caller with no package) and with the router's `callerPackageId !== ''` guard. `RouteActionDeclaration` and `callerPackageId` in the runtime are fine and not on the barrel.
- **Deviation 1, "no new resolver; owner-scoped VIEW fed to R."** Confirmed in the tree: `actionOwnerScopedRegistry` wraps the five `PackageScopedRegistry` reads and filters `action` items by `standaloneActionOwnerKey`; steps, closure and refusals are R's. The card's "read the resolver through those exports only, never re-implement the rule" (6728348521) holds.
- **Deviation 2, ruling B interim for the no-package same-object pair.** Confirmed pinned (objectql `[#31697 interim]`, runtime `[#31697 interim]`), code comment cites #31697, the unqualified slot's code is unchanged. Census 0 on the four first-party compositions is the dev's reading on the branch; the ruling's "stop if non-zero" was honoured on it.
- **Deviation 3, no door passes `callerPackageId`.** Confirmed: the narrowing arms are reachable by no request on this head. Both declared arms are real at the declaration layer (`resolveActionByPackage` and the router's refusal, pinned in both packages); the handler layer has the F1 hole.
- **Deviation 4, root eslint over the two packages instead of per-package `lint`.** Process; `Lint · ESLint` on this head is `success`.
- **Flag: the claim's Responsibility line said "the first registered answers"; measured "last registered runs, first declaration served".** Correct reading of `main`'s `registerAction` (replace and warn) and of rung 1's first-wins dedup; the record adopts the measured reading.
- **`ActionNavItem` half of the card.** No reader exists in objectql or runtime (ruling 6728550494 agreed); E2's share is the `/actions` door's resolution, delivered. The Console's half: the PR body names U #31671 as a carrier, but the epic registration (#31527 body) records U closed `not_planned` with its carriers on G1 #31691 and G3 #31695. Prose only (PR body); the seat may correct it when it accepts.
- **Out-of-scope finding (ADR-0150 coverage table counts action as phase-1 covered; phase 1 covers object-less actions only).** Carried to child A #31685 per the ruling; not this record's.
- **Red line 3 readings.** (a) phase-1 one-holder tests: unmeasured by CI on this head (cancelled), dev-reported green; (b) bare behaviour unchanged for every name with one holder: by construction (no-package path byte-identical) and pinned; (c) no migration; (d) declaration present and read.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main` (ADR-0150 D3, D3 (a), D4, D5; red lines 1 to 3) and the cited code. Does it take a declared capability away at the consumer, or make the spec's own refusal real?

**What holds.**
- D3 (a) is made real where the ADR puts it: a package caller's bare `(objectName, name)` resolves through R over an owner-scoped view; an environment-only holder is refused `outside-closure` naming the environment (pinned objectql and runtime), a closure double is refused naming both, an outside-closure package is refused naming it, and a refusal on the object never falls through to object-less holders (pinned). Nothing is narrowed at a consumer; the refusal is the spec's own.
- D4's key is real on both halves: two packages' handlers for one object and name coexist, a package call runs its own, withdrawal keeps the other's (pinned). Two objects under one name are two keys for every caller (pinned), which is the view's whole reason to exist.
- Red line 1 at the declaration layer: no first-match for a caller that names its package; the rungs are reached only when the registry view answers not-found. Red line 2: the 409 carries `message` and `candidates`. The no-package call keeps today's exact answer (interim B), so nothing today's consumers rely on moves.
- The lean core boundary holds without a workaround (R2 #31716 note respected).

**Findings.**

- **F1, should-fix: the handler fallback reaches an environment-authored action's handler for a package caller.** `packageScopedHandler` falls to "the one host-bound handler" by `handlerOwnerPackageId(owner) === owner`, which is true for owner `undefined` (host code), a plugin id, and `'metadata-service'`, the authored-action resync. The resync binds environment-authored actions whose name no code package ships, under `OBJECT:NAME` at coordinate `''`. Path: package P declares `approve` on `account` with `target: 'send'` and no body (no `app:P` handler); the environment authors `send` on `account` (resync-bound at `''`); G1 passes `callerPackageId: P`; the declaration resolves to P (`own`), `resolveActionHandlerKeys` rotates to `send`, `executeAction('account', 'send', ctx, { packageId: P })` misses P's slot, finds one host-bound entry, and runs the environment's `send`. D3 (a) says a package item's bare reference whose only holder is the environment is refused; the handler index serves it. Today's no-package call does the same, so nothing loosens relative to `main`, and no door passes a package yet, which keeps it below must-fix. Fix: exclude entries whose `package` is the resync's owner from the fallback (or give the resync a coordinate distinct from host code), and pin "a package call never reaches an environment-authored handler". The dev's own pin names "never runs another package's handler" and does not cover this owner.
- **F2, should-fix: the owner gate judges the unqualified slot's handler while the dispatch runs the package slot's.** `actionHandlerOwnerRefusal` reads `listRegisteredActions()` (unqualified slot only) and keys the reached entry by `object:key`; with `declarationPackageId` the dispatched entry is the package slot's under the same key. On a same-object pair (P and B hold `account:approve`, a door passes P): P's handler runs, but B's declaration is read as an owner of the reached entry, so B's `requiredPermissions` and B's activation switch gate P's call, and the refusal text names B. Over-refusal only (never a loosening), bounded by the #31697 pair (census 0) and by no door passing a package. Fix: have the owner reading take the dispatch's coordinate (compare the entry's owner coordinate with `declarationPackageId`, or let `listRegisteredActions` enumerate coordinates). N4 is the same blindness in the inventory readers.
- **N1, nit: `coordinateOfUnqualified`'s identity loop never matches.** `placeHandler` and the unqualified `set` create separate entry objects, as does each `bind` in `registerActionOverride`, so `slot.get(key) === entry` is never true and the function always answers `actionHandlerCoordinate(entry.package)`. Right for a plain registration; for a no-`base` override placed over an existing override it names the override's own coordinate, not the base's where that override was bound. Unreached: the resync always passes `base`.
- **N2, nit, follow-up: `IObjectQLEngine.executeAction` stays three-arity** while the dispatcher calls four on `any`. A contract-conforming substitute engine would drop `packageId` silently and run the unqualified handler for a package call. The card forbids a spec edit; a `domain:spec` follow-up (or G1, Clause-② yes) widens the contract with the optional `options`.
- **N3, nit, note for G1: the not-found fallthrough.** When the registry view holds no `action` item of the name, a package caller takes `main`'s rungs (object-embedded first match, then the protocol's unqualified by-name read). On a host whose authored rows are not hydrated into the registry (the rung the code names "env-scoped kernels where the registry carries no copy") that read can serve an environment row to a package caller. Common kernels hydrate `sys_metadata` into the registry, where the view refuses; G1 should pin the other shape or state it.
- **N4, nit: `listRegisteredActions`, the ADR-0110 D5 inventory (`reconcileActionRegistrations`) and the `hasRegisteredHandler` probe see the unqualified slot only.** On `main` a replaced handler vanished; now it lives on in a package slot and runs for a package caller while every inventory reader cannot name it. No answer today changes.
- **N5, nit, prose: the PR body names U #31671 as the Console's carrier;** U is closed `not_planned` (epic registration), carriers G1 #31691 and G3 #31695. Prose face only.

Grading: no must-fix. F1 and F2 earn a delta review of their fix; a fix anywhere but the prose faces moves the head, and this record then covers `d49c1e0d` only. The branch already carries `bff4bd5b` ("a package call's handler fallback reaches plugin handlers only, and refuses two"), which touches F1's exact seam and is outside this record.
